heading: Absolute agreement
gloss: raters give the same score

heading: Average-unit ICC: `ICC(*,k)`
gloss: the reliability of a mean of several raters

heading: Burch interval
gloss: a closed-form interval with a kurtosis adjustment

heading: Confidence interval vs. credible interval
gloss: holds the share of the posterior probability that the confidence level sets

heading: Conflated ICC
gloss: the single-level ICC that ignores clustering

heading: Connectedness (identification)
gloss: raters and subjects form one linked web

heading: Consistency
gloss: raters agree apart from a constant offset per rater

heading: Credible interval
gloss: see the confidence-interval entry

heading: Dependability coefficient
gloss: the generalizability-theory name for the agreement ICC

heading: D-study (decision study)
gloss: projects the fitted variance components to other rater or occasion counts

heading: Effective number of ratings: `k_eff`
gloss: the harmonic mean of the per-subject rating counts

heading: Engine
gloss: the software that does the fitting

heading: Estimand
gloss: the true quantity you are trying to estimate

heading: Exact-F interval
gloss: a closed-form interval that assumes normal data

heading: FIML
gloss: uses every observed value rather than dropping incomplete cases

heading: Finite-population rater variance: `θ²_r`
gloss: the spread of just the observed raters

heading: Fixed vs. random raters
gloss: the observed raters are the whole population of interest

heading: Harmonic mean
gloss: an average that leans toward the smaller values

heading: Indicator-mean estimator
gloss: reads the rater variance from the estimated column means

heading: Modified profile likelihood
gloss: profiles the likelihood in the ICC with a small-sample correction

heading: Monte-Carlo interval
gloss: built by drawing parameter values from the fitted model's uncertainty

heading: Occasion (within-cell replicate)
gloss: one of several ratings by the same rater of the same subject

heading: `occasions` vs. `n_o`
gloss: two column names, both code

heading: One-way vs. two-way
gloss: each rater is tracked across the subjects they score

heading: Parametric bootstrap
gloss: refits the model on simulated data many times

heading: Posterior mode (MAP)
gloss: the peak of the posterior distribution

heading: Prior
gloss: the distribution placed on a parameter before seeing the data

heading: REML
gloss: a way to estimate variances that corrects maximum likelihood's downward bias

heading: Single-unit ICC: `ICC(*,1)`
gloss: the reliability of one rater's score

heading: Subject level vs. cluster level
gloss: the subject level is reliability within a cluster, and the cluster level is reliability of cluster means

heading: Transformed bootstrap-*t*
gloss: resamples whole subjects and studentizes

heading: Variance component
gloss: a share of the total variation traced to one source

heading: Zero-variance boundary
gloss: an estimate can land exactly at zero

heading: References
gloss: the reference list
